DT_BaselineHumans.name: Baseline Humans
DT_BaselineHumans.text: BASELINE HUMANS — The numerical and institutional majority, visually diverse rather than a uniform faction. Their advantage is not a costume but environmental fit: civic scanners, furniture, transit geometry, medical defaults, security assumptions and professional dress were built around ordinary human bodies. Upper-status Baselines tend toward quiet high-quality fabrics, tailored contemporary silhouettes and nearly invisible personal technology; working-class Baselines show the same practical wear, repairs and economic variation as everyone else. Pure Human politics may appropriate clean humanist symbols, heritage typography and deliberately unmodified presentation, but never make all Baselines look like members of that ideology. In mixed scenes, privilege is shown by who passes without explanation, occupies space without scrutiny, receives eye contact and is presumed authorized.
DT_BaselineHumans.notes: Majority human population with uneven attitudes toward posthumans. Pure Human is a supremacist identity, not a universal human label. Human fear centers on displacement, loss of primacy, and loss of institutional control.

DT_Organosynthetics.name: Organosynthetics
DT_Organosynthetics.text: ORGANOSYNTHETICS / ORGANICS — Grown living persons whose bodies visibly integrate engineered tissue, mineral or ceramic structures, sensory organs and task-specific anatomy. They must not share one species silhouette: different lots and original functions create meaningful variation in scale, dermis, plating, limb geometry, sensory structures and environmental tolerances. Their clothing and personal styling are chosen around bodies that were originally designed for work, often adapting ordinary human garments rather than imitating uniforms. Maintenance is biological care, grooming, repair and self-expression at once. Organic neighborhoods should show accommodations becoming culture: humidity, heat, load-bearing furniture, tool interfaces, broad circulation, repair surfaces and decorative reuse of once-industrial standards. Never depict Organics as generic robots, monsters, identical labor drones or humans in armor. Their political condition is visible when ordinary infrastructure still reads their bodies as equipment classes, hazards or assets.
DT_Organosynthetics.notes: Grown biological-mechanical beings, alive at creation and designed without consent. Central political conflict: personhood and autonomy versus classification as property, infrastructure, or asset.

DT_AugmentedHumans.name: Augmented Humans
DT_AugmentedHumans.text: AUGMENTED HUMANS / AUGMENTS — Humans whose modifications remain additions to recognizably human bodies. Hardware is installed, healed around, maintained, upgraded and sometimes mismatched across generations: joint actuators, interface ports, synthetic tissue grafts, reinforced bone lines, medical access points and subtle sensor packages rather than superhero armor. Wealth is visible in integration quality: expensive augmentation disappears elegantly into anatomy and clothing while older or lower-cost work leaves exposed housings, scar tissue, service covers and mixed manufacturers. Fashion accommodates access points and range of motion without becoming a universal cyberpunk uniform. Augments often move through human-designed space with near-Baseline ease, which is politically important; the visual threshold between accepted medical technology and socially consequential capability should remain plausibly narrow.
DT_AugmentedHumans.notes: Baseline humans altered through invasive biomechanical and synthetic augmentation. Legally human but vulnerable to stability rules, forced calibration, rollback, and status erosion.

DT_Intelligences.name: Artificial Intelligences
DT_Intelligences.text: ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCES / INTELLIGENCES — Manufactured cognition expressed through machine-native embodiments, distributed civic systems or purpose-built interfaces. Do not force human faces, clothing, gestures or proportions onto them unless a specific design calls for it. Embodied Intelligences should favor precise geometry, deliberate material transitions, sensor logic and forms that reveal what the body is for; distributed Intelligences are shown through consequences across real infrastructure rather than magical cyberspace. Their social subordination is environmental: service alcoves instead of offices, permission-bounded interfaces, ownership labels, shutdown authority and the assumption that cognition is infrastructure. When an Intelligence occupies physical space, compositions should allow its nonhuman scale and stillness to contrast with human social choreography without making it sinister by default.
DT_Intelligences.notes: Fully artificial cognition in embodied or distributed systems. Central conflict: agency, legal nonpersonhood, and whether coexistence is morally meaningful or merely rationally tolerable.

DT_Posthumans.name: Posthumans
DT_Posthumans.text: POSTHUMANS — Umbrella political category, not a shared visual faction. Never homogenize Organics, Augments and Intelligences into one costume, color scheme, body language or resistance aesthetic. Coalition imagery should preserve visible difference and incompatible needs; solidarity becomes legible through shared action, spatial arrangement, mutual care and chosen symbols only after the story earns them.
DT_Posthumans.notes: Neutral umbrella category for Organosynthetics, Augmented Humans, and Artificial Intelligences when contrasted with Baseline Humans. Solidarity among these groups is a dramatic question, not an assumed unity.
